title: Word 28 — On Eternal Torment and Eternal Life
attribution_note: Word 28 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Even the worst earthly misery has some comfort

pairs.en: Just as eternal blessedness can, in some small measure, be known and felt through temporal misfortune, so too can eternal misfortune be known through temporal suffering. There is no calamity so great in this world that carries no comfort or relief at all. Poverty is grievous, but it finds comfort in the name of Christ and in the mercy of good people. Cruel sickness is tormenting, but it is eased by medicine or other remedy. It is counted a great calamity and misfortune to lose not only honor, possessions, wife, and children, but even to be cast into prison. Yet even one suffering so is not without comfort: he enjoys the light and air common to all, though not equally with the free man; he is refreshed by food and drink, forgets his burden in sleep, is comforted by the visits of good people, and is nourished by the hope of release. Perhaps he does not even suffer wounds or beatings. If he suffers unjustly, he is cheered by the hope of a heavenly reward; and if justly, he humbles himself before God, acknowledges his sin, repents, and so is refreshed by the hope of God's mercy, saying: *“It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I might learn Your statutes”* [Psalm 118:71]. And more than this — death will bring it all to an end.

sections.heading: What it means to be cast out from the glory of Christ

pairs.en: But how grievous, how unbearable it is to be deprived of that glory before which all the glory of this world is as filth! To lose the sight of that beautiful Face, whose beauty, loveliness, and grace turn the whole heart and spirit into desire and love — of whom the blessed spirits have never from the beginning had their fill, and to eternity will never cease being filled without ever being sated! To be cast away from Christ the King of glory, whose beauty surpasses the shining of the sun, of whose sweetness Saint Peter, having tasted but a little on the mountain, cried out: *“It is good for us to be here”* [Matthew 17:4]! To be driven away from that beautiful heavenly city, Jerusalem, which *“has no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illumines it, and its lamp is the Lamb”* [Revelation 21:23]. To be banished from that glorious and sweet supper, at which from the beginning of the world to its end *“the called and chosen of God will sing, rejoice, and cry out for joy”* [Isaiah 65:14]! To be cut off from the beloved fellowship of the blessed spirits and all the saints, and, worse still, to be numbered among the dark and cunning spirits; to be shut up in a prison, never to see the light; to suffer without relief in the fire of Gehenna, which burns but does not consume, torments but does not kill!

sections.heading: Temporal suffering ends; eternal misfortune does not

pairs.en: Temporal calamity and suffering, as has been said, whatever form it takes, is never without some comfort, and however long it lasts, it ends with death — but that other calamity and misfortune is without end! There will be no return to the glory of God, no deliverance from the chains of hell and the torment of fire; in a word, it is eternal despair of God's mercy, an eternal sensing of the righteous wrath of God. There the answer will be heard: *“Remember that you in your lifetime received your good things”* [Luke 16:25].

sections.heading: The second death: always dying, never dead

pairs.en: Here people flee from death, but there they will long for it — and it will flee from them; they will wish to be turned to nothing, but will not be able to, and so they will always be dying, yet never die: this is *“the second death”* [Revelation 20:14]. This intense suffering is made still greater in that the sufferer is left with no hope of ever recovering the good he lost through his own negligence, or of ever being freed from the terrible evil into which he fell of his own will. From this will follow the greatest anguish, the greatest fear and terror; conscience will rise up and, through all eternity, will accuse and gnaw at the sinner for having rejected so great a grace of God, for having so willfully deprived himself forever of God's highest mercy, and for having brought himself to so tormented a state.

sections.heading: God's love rejected, God's mercy no longer heard

pairs.en: God, the Creator of heaven and earth, did not spare His own Son for your sake, but delivered Him to death and to bitter suffering, as the Gospel has declared to you and the teachers of the Church have preached. And God did this in order to deliver you from that calamity. But you despised this ineffable love of God; for the sake of some small, passing pleasure you abandoned God, followed your own whims rather than the will of God who wished to save you, and served and pleased satan rather than Christ.

sections.heading: Others rejoice while you perish — the wasted calls to repentance

pairs.en: Behold, other people just like you are now comforted, rejoicing, filled with eternal blessings, because they believed and by faith followed Christ their Savior — but you rejected the counsel of God, and so you have perished! How many times did God call you to repentance! How many times did preachers exhort you! You despised it all. You did not wish to listen to God in your lifetime, and now God will not listen to you either. Expect nothing more than the calamity in which you now find yourself. You will drink this cup of bitterness forever, yet never drink it dry. Repent now — but it is too late and useless, since you did not wish to repent to good purpose while you lived. Groan, sigh, weep, wail — but it is useless, since you did not wish to weep there, where tears were of use!

sections.heading: The conscience that never stops gnawing; the dread of eternity itself

pairs.en: O eternity, eternity, woeful eternity! How even the mere thought of you terrifies our spirit! As much as blessed eternity delights and enraptures the spirit of one who ponders it, so much does woeful eternity bring it to sorrow and dread. It is impossible to think of this latter eternity without sighing and terror.

sections.heading: Better any earthly suffering than that eternity

pairs.en: For here, whatever suffering befalls, each kind of it has some comfort and ends with death; but there, the suffering — the fierce suffering — is without any comfort at all, a suffering not only beyond words but beyond the mind's grasp; a suffering that will always be, yet never ends: *“their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched,”* says the prophet [Isaiah 66:24]. Whoever believes this, pondering and often recalling this dreadful misfortune, may be roused to more fervent repentance, that he might be delivered from that calamity; but whoever does not believe it will in fact taste its bitterness, and, as has been said, will taste it without end.

sections.heading: The final separation: eternal life and eternal torment

pairs.en: Both go forth, but not alike: some with weeping and inconsolable wailing, others with joy and unspeakable rejoicing. For they go to unequal places: some into the mansions of the Heavenly Father, into the adorned halls of the King of glory, to the great supper of endless delight, and to the most sweet marriage feast of the Lamb; others into the eternal prison and the place of weeping, wailing, and the fiercest torment. Some heaven will receive with all its blessings, *“which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man”* [1 Corinthians 2:9]; others hell will shut in with all its evils, which we can neither describe in words nor comprehend in mind. Amen.
